 Have owned a technical product from a blank repo to something people actually used.

 We're looking for an Escalation Engineer to join the Cockroach Labs Technical Support team in the AMER region.  Familiarity with, or willingness to learn, the technologies behind enterprise applications. 
 The ability to absorb information. You love getting into the weeds technically, but don't let that distract you from achieving your goals. 
 The ability to participate in a weekend on-call rotation.

You'll work closely with Product, Design, and engineering leadership, and partner with teams across the organization to build, iterate, and scale meaningful solutions. You'll have the autonomy to guide what we build and how, and the influence to bring others along with you, all while staying hands-on in the codebase. 
 We're looking for thoughtful engineers who enjoy owning problems end to end, collaborating across disciplines, and solving complex technical challenges for products that millions of developers rely on every day. AI is a foundational part of how we build, so we value engineers who are excited to thoughtfully incorporate AI-assisted workflows while continuing to apply strong engineering fundamentals. We believe the best engineering happens when talented people are trusted to solve difficult problems together, share what they're learning, and create space for different perspectives to shape better solutions.  With our team, you'll have real ownership from day one - not a tiny slice of a massive codebase. Engineers here are trusted to make decisions, shape technical direction, and move quickly while collaborating closely with Product and Design. 
  What You'll Do  
 
 Use your deep expertise in full-stack development (TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, and React) to ship reliable, scalable, performant code across our product suite, and set the patterns that others on the team and across the org follow.  
 Own the technical direction for our product area, including the web app, CLI, MCP, SDK, API, and docs, by defining architecture and roadmap alongside your manager, Product, and Design, and make tradeoffs explicit so decisions are easy to understand and revisit 
 Lead large, ambiguous projects that span multiple teams from conception to delivery, such as our application rewrite and upcoming CLI rework, writing RFCs, driving alignment, and managing risk and timelines 
 Design and evolve user-facing features and product APIs for both humans and agents, recognizing that the best interface isn’t always a React application. Build them to scale to millions of developers worldwide, with a clear view of reliability, performance, and long-term maintainability. 
 Make thoughtful product and interface decisions on your own with the overall customer experience top of mind

 Mentor and grow engineers through code reviews, design reviews, pairing, and sponsorship, raising the technical level of the whole team 
 Practice proactive async communication and create visibility across projects by documenting your workflows and decision-making clearly

 Collaborate with cross-functional teams and engineering leadership to shape user flows that enhance the developer experience across our platform, and contribute to hiring and team growth 
 
  What You'll Bring  
 
 Deep expertise in TypeScript and JavaScript, with a long track record of designing, shipping, and maintaining production-quality software in modern full-stack environments 
 A history of building interfaces developers use directly, such as web apps, CLIs, APIs, SDKs, or other dev tools, and a strong sense of what works well for developers (and, by extension, agents) 
 Passion for building strong user-facing experiences, including working with React and modern frontend architecture and making architectural decisions that hold up as products and teams grow, paired with the backend knowledge to design software well beyond the UI 
 Strong product and design instincts. This isn’t about visual polish - it’s about making thoughtful decisions about how users interact

 About the role 
 For 40 years Vertican has buildt software that runs law firms. One year ago we created a new modern AI platform for document automation (processing/extraction/redacting) which our customers have been adopting faster than any product we've ever had. Our suite of AI-enabled products save customers thousands of hours each week by processing high volumes of documents with precision and speed.The AI team is growing and we'd like you to join. 
 We are hiring an engineer to own the document processing pipelines end to end: design, benchmarking, experimenting with new architectures and tools, threshold required for deploying a new pipeline, etc. 
 We believe it's important to build our own tooling to help us run, improve, and measure our applications. Therefore, the ideal candidate thinks outside the box on how to not just build the product/pipeline, but also the tooling needed around it. 
 You will be the first dedicated ML hire on the product taking over from the engineering manager who build the current solution and will work directly with the founding engineering team. 
 This is a senior, hands-on individual-contributor role, but we are small team and you'll be involved in design, planning, roadmapping, and architectural decisions. 
 What you will do 
  Design the pipelines.  Own the architecture of the extraction-to-posting pipelines: page classification, field extraction, candidate retrieval, claim matching, confidence gating and the hand-off to human review, etc. Decide where rules end and models begin, and what each stage must guarantee to the next, what the separation of concerns are, etc. 
 We have different pipelines for different document types and expect that at any given point in time we may have new ones emerge and may consolidate others. 
  Evaluate new systems before we adopt them.  Run structured trials of candidate components and recommend what to keep. Examples include probabilistic record linkage (Splink), Azure AI Content Understanding and Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI and Foundry-hosted models, and LLM agents with tools. Similarly, test new models with the existing pipeline as they are relased from the frontier labs. 
  Build the evaluation process.  You'll own the process of evaluating false positives, false negatives, errors of ommission, etc, that we ultimately use to determine if we should upgrade the pipeline.  
  Ship and operate.  Take components from trial to production in our python workers on the cloud, instrument them, watch cost and quota, and diagnose the cases reviewers send back. 
  Set direction.  Work with leadereship on the planing for accuracy, cost improvement, and overall product improvements. 
 What we are looking for 
  Required  
 
 6+ years building ML or data-intensive systems, at least 3 of them owning a production pipeline whose output people acted on. 
 Solid backend engineering understanding and ideally cloud architecture understanding. 
 Ideally hands-on experience with document understanding: OCR or layout models, field extraction from scanned PDFs, or intelligent document processing products. 
 Experience with entity resolution or record linkage at scale (Splink, Dedupe, Zingg, or your own blocking-and-scoring system) against databases of hundreds of thousands of rows. 
 You have designed an evaluation from scratch: built a labeled ground-truth set, chosen the metrics, and defended a threshold to a non-technical stakeholder. 
 Production experience with LLM APIs, including structured output, tool calling and cost or rate-limit management; you can say when an LLM is the wrong tool. 
 Strong Python and SQL. Comfortable reading Postgres query plans and writing the raw query when the ORM gets in the way. 
 Engineering/Scientist mindset: you are scientific about testing the pipeline and how results are interpeted/presented. 
 
  Nice to have  
 
 Azure AI services (Content Understanding, Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI, Foundry) or the AWS and GCP equivalents. 
 Financial document processing: checks, remittance advices, lockbox files, payment matching, or accounts receivable automation. 
 Exposure to collections, legal operations or other regulated workflows handling PII.
